title: I Took the Alpaca-Halter Checkout to the Chair Who Skipped the Fiber Log

parts.text: I stepped into the fiber barn at 8:09 a.m. and chair Ines was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE HALTER. THIRTY MINUTES. FIBER STAYS WITH THE CHECKOUT. I was twenty-nine, farm secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered fiber bags. Ines shrugged. "Chairs are the fiber." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover bags on my numbered halter. Then I asked for the fiber log. At 8:17 the barn pinged why Ines's name was on my bags. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The barn can see Ines's leftover bags on my numbered halter.

social.video_title: She skipped the fiber log on my alpaca halter — Part 1/2
social.description: Fiber barn, leftover bags, a thirty-minute clock she posted. I logged the fiber. Would you have asked for the fiber log?

parts.text: Ines called it skirting until the barn asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the bag still. The fiber went back to my numbered checkout. Ines ran a slot of her own and told the next chair atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE FIBER. I keep my bags on a labeled shelf. Ines brown-bags her skirting. The barn finally looks like a checkout, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Fiber log, numbered halter, and a second line on the board. Was skirting ever my bags?
